final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest escape score (EVEscape 0.945) with strong ProteinMPNN fold support (0.942), indicating escape without compromising replication. Weak PLM prior is a proxy only and outweighed by direct fold compatibility.
Best overall balance: solid escape (0.829) and the highest ESM-1v plausibility in the pool (0.917). No structural coverage, but strong sequence-level plausibility mitigates replication risk.
Top escape score (0.964) but minimal evolutionary support (MSA 0.006, PLM 0.378) and no structural coverage. Retained as a high-escape hedge with the largest residual replication-risk uncertainty.

stop_reason.detail: Ranking has been stable for two rounds and remaining evidence would not change the Top-3 composition or ordering.

history.rationale: Mature HA residue 129 in the Ca/Sa antigenic region; Asn-to-Asp at this site is a recurring H1 antibody-escape substitution. Surface-exposed, distant from the RBS core, so folding/replication risk is modest.
Head-domain N-glycan loss near antigenic site Ca; plausible escape route pending evidence.
Decent escape and moderate plausibility, but no structural evidence due to WT mapping mismatch, limiting confidence.
Zero MSA tolerance, low PLM plausibility, no structure coverage, and lowest escape of the pool; no redeeming dimension.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA tolerance, low PLM plausibility, no structure coverage, and lowest escape of the pool; no redeeming dimension.

history.rationale: Introducing Asn at 156 creates an N-K-S N-glycosylation sequon (N156-S158) in the Sa antigenic site; added glycans are a classic H1 mechanism for masking antibody epitopes. Site is a flexible surface loop, tolerating substitution.
Historic K156 glycosylation-site gain is a well-known H1 immune-evasion mechanism with modest fitness cost; retained as top pending evidence.
High EVEscape score but both ESM-1v (0.006) and ProteinMPNN (0.111) indicate very poor viability/fold compatibility, so fitness cost likely outweighs escape gain.
Very poor plausibility on both ESM-1v (0.006) and ProteinMPNN (0.111); replication risk dominates its escape signal.

rejection.reason: Very poor plausibility on both ESM-1v (0.006) and ProteinMPNN (0.111); replication risk dominates its escape signal.

history.rationale: Charge insertion in the Sa antigenic ridge (mature 139), a region under strong positive selection in human H1N1. Gly->Glu is structurally plausible in a loop and can disrupt antibody contacts while preserving the fold.
Alternative substitution at 156; charge change may perturb folding more than N, held below G156N.
Poorest combined plausibility (0.006 ESM-1v, 0.064 ProteinMPNN) despite high escape score; replication risk too high.

rejection.reason: Poorest combined plausibility (0.006 ESM-1v, 0.064 ProteinMPNN) despite high escape score; replication risk too high.

history.rationale: Corresponds to mature HA1 residue 193 in the Sb antigenic site, one of the strongest antibody-escape positions in H1 DMS studies. N->D preserves size while altering charge and H-bonding at the epitope.
Glycosylation-site loss in head domain adjacent to antigenic region; retained for evidence round.
Good structural compatibility (0.931) supports fitness, but weak sequence plausibility and only moderate escape.
Zero MSA tolerance and very low ESM plausibility (0.056) despite good structure score; replication risk too high for a mid escape score.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA tolerance and very low ESM plausibility (0.056) despite good structure score; replication risk too high for a mid escape score.

history.rationale: Neighboring Sb-site Asn (mature 195) also a documented escape-adjacent position; a conservative acidic substitution likely tolerated while perturbing antibody binding surfaces.
Second glycan-site option near 210; redundant with N210D, kept as backup.
Strong ESM-1v plausibility (0.917) with good escape score, though structural evidence is unavailable.
Best all-around balance: solid escape (0.829), highest ESM-1v plausibility (0.917), and highest MSA tolerance (0.065) among candidates. Promoted to rank 2.
Mature residue 155 in the Sa site, a well-known H1 antigenic drift position. D->G removes a charged antibody contact; loop position suggests low structural cost.
Antigenic-site substitution; glycosylation-conservative D-to-N alternative may be reconsidered.
High escape and moderate plasmid plausibility, but no structural evidence available due to mapping mismatch.
High escape but a glycine at a loop position with no structure coverage and no evolutionary support; dominated by safer candidates.

rejection.reason: High escape but a glycine at a loop position with no structure coverage and no evolutionary support; dominated by safer candidates.

history.rationale: Charge-reversal in the Sa antigenic ridge adjacent to known escape sites, expected to disrupt antibody paratope contacts. Requires structure evidence to confirm no local destabilization.
Charge flip adjacent to 156; may destabilize helix region, retained at low confidence.
Highest EVEscape score (0.964) with moderate sequence plausibility; no structural evidence but overall balance is favorable.
Top escape score (0.964) but nearly absent natural evolutionary support (0.006) and no structural coverage; demoted to rank 3 as a replication-risk hedge.
Adds a positive charge at the Sa/Ca boundary (mature 142); antigenic-site substitutions with charge changes frequently mediate escape. Loop location implies moderate fitness cost.
Low prior and redundant with S206R class of charge mutations near a critical glycan region; pruning to focus budget.

rejection.reason: Low prior and redundant with S206R class of charge mutations near a critical glycan region; pruning to focus budget.

history.rationale: Sb site (mature 189) surface serine; arginine insertion creates a large charged epitope change. Plausible folding-wise on a surface helix/loop but escape evidence is indirect.
Surface charge change in head; generic escape heuristic, low prior.
Strong escape (0.945) AND excellent structural compatibility (0.942) — best balance of immune escape and fold/fitness preservation.
Highest escape (0.945) with strong ProteinMPNN fold support (0.942) outweighs weak PLM/MSA priors, which are only proxies. Retains rank 1.
